n.story:
The traditional image of the locker room attendant is being replaced by a role focused on facility hospitality and high-level problem solving. Routine tasks like allocating locker space and managing lost-and-found logs have been almost entirely automated through smart-lock systems and image-recognition databases. This frees you from the 'desk' and places you on the floor as a proactive service provider.

Your value now lies in your ability to manage the physical environment and handle complex human interactions that sensors cannot. While a robot might scrub a large open floor, you are the one ensuring the safety of cluttered spaces and providing a human face to customer service. You use AI as a digital assistant to monitor facility needs in real-time, allowing you to intervene before a customer even notices a problem.

You become a service coordinator, using AI to manage the flow of people and items while you provide the human connection that defines a premium experience.
